title: India news: British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal granted bail after 9 years in detention
content:
India: British Sikh man granted bail after 9-year detention
Published September 19, 2026last updated September 19, 2026What you need to know
- Scottish-Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal, who had been detained in India for almost nine years without being convicted, has been granted bail
- India is set to replace Asian Games opening ceremony male flagbearer over missing ceremonial kit
- Counting underway in elections for the Delhi University Students' Union
Here is a roundup of some of the top headlines from across India on Saturday, September 19:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
We are pausing our coverage
Over 10 years after my last day as a Delhi University student, I will wrap up this Saturday's coverage of events with the 2026 DUSU elections.
But we will be back tomorrow, so follow DW for more!
WATCH — Basmati rice: India, Pakistan and the race for recognition
One of the world's most valuable rice varieties, basmati carries strong historic ties to the Punjab region, which spans both India and Pakistan.
Both claim the premium, aromatic rice as part of their agriculture and cultural heritage, and are seeking European Union recognition for its geographical origin.
But years after the first application was filed in 2018, the fight over basmati rice is far from over.
Watch for more:
ABVP sweeps DUSU polls as student safety, identity dominate campaign
The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), affiliated with the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its ideological parent Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), won three of four central posts in this year's Delhi University Students' Union elections, with its candidate Yash Dabas coming in from behind to be elected president.
Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen made history by winning the vice-presidential seat, defeating candidates fielded by both ABVP and the National Students' Union of India (NSUI), the student wing of the Indian National Congress.
In a university facing an acute shortage of hostels, student housing and safety dominated this year's campaign. This came after the September 6 collapse of a paying-guest building in Satya Niketan, near Delhi University's South Campus, which killed seven students.
High rents, non-functional hostels, and a lack of affordable lodging near campus were central issues in candidate platforms.
Declaring his win, Dabas stressed the issue as he addressed the media: "We all witnessed the accident that occurred in Satya Niketan; we do not want such an incident to happen to anyone in the future, and that will be our first priority — conducting safety audits for every college, hostel, and PG."
Shokeen, an NSUI rebel who ran independently, built his campaign partly around the tragedy, vowing not to wear footwear until affected students got justice.
The election also unfolded in the shadow of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led satirical protest movement that organized weeks of demonstrations at Delhi's Jantar Mantar earlier this year, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in national entrance exams.
While the CJP was not involved in the DUSU race directly, the movement shaped how many voters approached the election.
"Students were talking about what or ganisations stand for, whether they agree with their politics and whether voting can give them a greater say in issues concerning students," one student told news agency PTI, adding that many felt they "should not simply vote because a particular organisation has always been influential on campus."
More uncertainty for Indian workers as Trump extends $100,000 H-1B visa fee
US President Donald Trump has extended the $100,000 fee on H-1B visa petitions through September 2027, the White House has said — a move that will be strongly felt in India, the largest source of H-1B recipients.
The extension, announced on Friday, keeps a policy first introduced in September 2025 in place. It excludes visa renewals and student visa holders transitioning to H-1B status.
Trump also signed a proclamation directing tighter scrutiny of applications, instructing agencies to weigh employers' recent layoffs of American workers when reviewing petitions.
The policy remains under legal challenge, with an appeals court reviewing a June ruling that found the fee unlawful.
The stakes are high for India: USCIS data for fiscal year 2025 showed Indian nationals accounted for 69.9% of approved H-1B petitions, far ahead of China's 12.1%.
When the fee first launched last year, it caused panic among Indian travelers, including passengers who deboarded a Delhi-bound flight fearing they'd be barred from returning.
Opposition Congress party leader Pawan Khera criticized the extension on social media, warning it would make it "harder for Indian students to enter the US workforce" and could drive a "talent drain" toward the UK, Canada and Australia.
He also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his perceived camaraderie with Trump, adding: "Modi bent over backwards to appease Trump. Trump got the appeasement. India took the humiliation and the hit."
Surendra Koli, acquitted in Nithari serial killings case, found dead in suspected suicide
Surendra Koli, a key figure in India's notorious 2006 Nithari serial killings case who was acquitted of all charges last year, was found dead at a tea stall he operated in Haridwar.
Police are treating the case as a suspected suicide.
Residents discovered Koli's body inside the rented stall and alerted authorities, Haridwar City Deputy Superintendent of Police Shishupal Singh Negi told local media.
No suicide note was found and the body was sent for post-mortem examination as investigators look into the circumstances.
Koli first drew national attention in 2006, when he was a domestic worker at businessman Moninder Singh Pandher's home in Noida. The discovery of human remains, including children's, in a drain behind Pandher's house sparked a major investigation and nationwide outrage.
Koli was convicted and sentenced to death in multiple cases beginning in 2009. In October 2023, the Allahabad High Court acquitted both Koli and Pandher for lack of evidence.
Two key observations were made: Koli's confession was inadmissible, as it was extracted after a long, unauthorized interrogation in police custody without adequate legal safeguards, and the prosecution could not prove that the remains uncovered from the "open, public" drain were based solely on Koli's statements.
The decision was upheld by India's Supreme Court in late 2025.
Reports suggest he moved to the northern city of Haridwar after the acquittal. Police identified Koli through an Aadhaar card found on his body.
India swaps flagbearer for Asian Games opening ceremony after kit mix-up
A last-minute logistics problem has cost shot-putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor his spot as India's male flagbearer at Saturday's Asian Games opening ceremony in Nagoya, Japan.
Kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat is set to step in instead, joining shooter Manu Bhaker, a two-time Paris Olympics bronze medalist, who will be India's female flagbearer.
Toor, who is chasing a third consecutive Asian Games gold in shot put, said he only learned of his selection as flagbearer a day earlier and that his kit was still back in India.
"I'm told that my kit will reach at 3 p.m. at the airport. Reaching the opening ceremony venue after collecting my kit from the airport on time will be very difficult," he told news agency PTI, adding that he had informed the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) that he would not be attending the ceremony.
The Indian Olympic Association said in a statement that Toor would be unable to serve as flagbearer "due to a technical issue."
The mix-up was one of several hiccups in the run-up to the Games, which open on Saturday with more than 17,000 athletes competing across more than 40 sports through October 4.
Organizers, working without a traditional athletes' village, have housed competitors in container-style huts, hotels and a cruise ship. There have been complaints over accommodation quality, transport delays, and a mistaken playing of North Korea's national anthem for South Korea's men's hockey team.
A tropical storm bearing down on the region threatens to cause further disruption as competition gets underway.
Delhi High Court grants bail to Jagtar Singh Johal after nearly nine years in custody
The Delhi High Court granted bail to British national Jagtar Singh Johal in seven murder and terrorism-related cases, clearing the way for his conditional release after nearly nine years in Indian custody.
The court overturned a 2024 ruling that had denied him bail.
Johal, 39, a Sikh rights campaigner from Dumbarton, Scotland, was arrested in Punjab in 2017 shortly after he arrived in India for his wedding.
He was accused by India's National Investigation Agency of financing and courier work for the banned Khalistan Liberation Force in connection with a series of targeted killings in Ludhiana and Jalandhar districts between 2016 and 2017.
He was acquitted in a related case last year by a court in Moga, Punjab, while the Delhi cases had continued.
Johal has consistently denied wrongdoing and says he was tortured into signing a false confession. A United Nations working group ruled in May 2022 that his detention was arbitrary.
"Eight and a half years of arbitrary detention without a clear path to trial is not justice, it is unlawful suffering," UN human rights experts said in a statement earlier this year. "The prolonged uncertainty alone is a form of psychological torture."
Indian authorities have repeatedly rejected the torture allegations and insisted that due process was followed.
What did the court say in its ruling?
In its ruling, the court cited Johal's prolonged incarceration and the slow pace of the trial as grounds for bail, despite the strict conditions typically imposed under India's anti-terror law, the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.
The court noted that 123 witnesses were yet to be examined and that proceedings were "certainly not likely to conclude any time soon."
The court imposed strict bail conditions, including surrendering his passport, restrictions on communication and social media activity, and regular reporting to the Investigating Officer. The court did not rule on the merits of the underlying case, leaving prosecutors free to have his bail revoked if the conditions of his release are breached.
Johal's brother, Gurpreet Singh Johal, who has campaigned for years for his release and urged successive UK governments to take action, called the ruling "a huge relief," the BBC reported.
"I had a long, sleepless night knowing that the decision would be made this morning. Now, all I can think about is Jagtar walking out of prison."
Welcome to our coverage
Hello! This is Seerat from DW's Studio Delhi, bringing you the big news from and about India this weekend.
We lead our coverage with the news that British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal, who had been detained in India for almost nine years without conviction, has been granted bail.
A UN panel in 2022 recognized it as a case of arbitrary detention, putting the Indian government's human rights record under the microscope.
The Asian Games kick off in Japan on Saturday, but it's not all smooth sailing for the Indian delegation's preparations.
India has announced a last-minute change of its male flagbearer for the opening ceremony after star shotputter Tajinderpal Singh Toor's ceremonial kit reportedly went missing.
Finally, counting is underway in elections for the Delhi University Student Union, this time under the shadow of the Cockroach Janata Party protests and the collapse of a building in the student hub of Satya Niketan.

title: «Σ’ αγαπώ πολύ μαμά μου» – Κινέζα νύφη έμαθε ελληνικά για να κάνει έκπληξη στην πεθερά της
content:
Μια πολύ όμορφη και συγκινητική έκπληξη ετοίμασε για την Ελληνίδα πεθερά της η Shu Lin. Η γυναίκα από την Κίνα αποφάσισε να μάθει ελληνικά κρυφά, ώστε να μπορέσει να της μιλήσει στη γλώσσα της κατά τη διάρκεια της γαμήλιας δεξίωσης στην Ελλάδα.
Η Shu Lin μοιράστηκε στα social media ένα βίντεο από τη συγκινητική στιγμή και εξήγησε την ιστορία πίσω από την προσπάθειά της. Όπως αποκάλυψε, ξεκίνησε να μαθαίνει ελληνικά από τον Απρίλιο. Η πεθερά της γνώριζε ότι έκανε μαθήματα ελληνικών, όμως δεν ήξερε τον πραγματικό λόγο για τον οποίο τα μάθαινε.
Η Shu Lin έλεγε στους φίλους και στους συγγενείς της ότι ήθελε να μάθει ελληνικά κυρίως για να μπορεί να παραγγέλνει φαγητό στα εστιατόρια. Η δικαιολογία αυτή είχε και μια δόση αλήθειας, αφού η αγάπη της για το φαγητό τη βοήθησε να μάθει περισσότερες ελληνικές λέξεις. Ωστόσο, ο πραγματικός της στόχος ήταν διαφορετικός: ήθελε να κρατήσει την εκμάθηση της γλώσσας μυστική, ώστε κανείς από τους Έλληνες φίλους και συγγενείς της να μην αποκαλύψει την έκπληξη.
Η μεγάλη στιγμή ήρθε στη γαμήλια δεξίωση, η οποία πραγματοποιήθηκε στην Ελλάδα, στην οικογενειακή ταβέρνα. Εκεί η Shu Lin κατάφερε να μιλήσει στην πεθερά της στα ελληνικά και να της πει όλα όσα είχε ετοιμάσει εδώ και μήνες.
Η ίδια περιγράφει την πεθερά της ως έναν άνθρωπο γεμάτο αγάπη, δύναμη, ζεστασιά, φροντίδα, γενναιοδωρία και χιούμορ. Από την πρώτη στιγμή, όπως αναφέρει, την υποδέχθηκε με πολλή αγάπη στην οικογένεια και την έκανε να νιώσει ευπρόσδεκτη.
Μέχρι να μάθει καλύτερα ελληνικά, οι δύο γυναίκες επικοινωνούσαν συχνά χρησιμοποιώντας το Google Translate. Η Shu Lin, όμως, συνέχισε να προσπαθεί και κατάφερε τελικά να μιλήσει στην πεθερά της στη μητρική της γλώσσα.
Με το μήνυμά της εξέφρασε την αγάπη, τον σεβασμό και την ευγνωμοσύνη της για τη γυναίκα που την υποδέχθηκε στην οικογένειά της. Ανάμεσα στα λόγια που της είπε ήταν και η φράση που συγκίνησε ιδιαίτερα: «Σ’ αγαπώ πολύ, μαμά μου».
Δείτε αυτή τη δημοσίευση στο Instagram.

title: « Toutes les charges sont comprises, il y a un espace de travail, une salle de détente, une laverie… » : quand les résidences étudiantes privées font le plein
content:
Cassandra a eu beau s’y prendre en février pour une rentrée en septembre, elle n’a pas eu l’embarras du choix. « J’ai commencé à chercher bien avant de savoir si j’étais acceptée par l’école, et il restait déjà très peu de logements disponibles », souligne l’étudiante en 2e année à l’institut de formation en soins infirmiers de Rouen (comme d’autres personnes interrogées, elle n’a pas souhaité donner son nom). Avec ses parents, et après cinq visites de studios en location dans le parc privé traditionnel, son choix s’est porté sur une résidence étudiante privée.
« Toutes les charges sont comprises, c’est sécurisé, il y a un espace de travail, une salle de détente, une laverie… », liste Cassandra, 19 ans. Son forfait comprend la location d’un studio de 26 mètres carrés ; la consommation d’eau chaude, d’électricité et de gaz ; l’accès aux espaces communs ; la fourniture du Wi-Fi et, cerise sur le gâteau, un service de ménage toutes les six semaines. La résidence se trouve à cinq minutes à pied de son école et du centre hospitalier universitaire. « Il y a deux sas pour accéder à la résidence et, sur place, deux étudiants qui sont référents en cas de problème. Ça a beaucoup rassuré mes parents », ajoute-t-elle.

title: Electricity Restored in El Condado After Protests Prompt Repair of Faulty Transformer
content:
Pressure from the residents of El Condado neighborhood in Santa Clara paid off: Following protests that blocked streets and erected barricades on Monday night, a technical crew from the Electric Company arrived to fix a faulty transformer that had left several blocks without power for almost 36 hours, according to a report by Martí Noticias.
The protest began with about 20 demonstrators on Estrada Palma Street and grew to over fifty participants, culminating days of mounting frustration. The transformer issue had already been reported to the state-run company, which had previously dispatched a crew that failed to solve the problem.
"They caused a commotion, and immediately, they came to fix the transformer," summarized Arnoldo Goicuña, a local resident, describing how the protest expedited the authorities' response.
Former political prisoner Liván Hernández Sosa, who lives in the community, explained the situation that led to the outburst: "A transformer had issues, it had been reported, and the [Electric Company's] truck had come, but the problem wasn't resolved. When they provided power to other areas for the two-hour supply, it didn't reach us because of the equipment's malfunction."
Escalating Tensions and Police Presence
Activist Guillermo del Sol confirmed that the protest quickly spread across the neighborhood: "It started in front of La Latina, but it became widespread. Many people sat on the sidewalks, and objects were set on fire."
There was police presence during the demonstration, but Hernández Sosa noted that he was not aware of any arrests being made.
Persistent Distrust Among Residents
Despite the restoration of service, mistrust among residents remains high. Hernández Sosa warned, "This repair will last a week, at most," highlighting the fragile infrastructure that has been deteriorating for months without structural solutions.
On social media, residents complained that El Condado has been without daytime electricity for five months, and the constant power fluctuations are damaging appliances. "No business can thrive," wrote one resident.
Recurring Pattern Across Cuba
The events in El Condado reflect a recurring pattern throughout Cuba: neighborhood protests as the only effective method to elicit a response from the government, even if it's temporary.
In El Fanguito, Havana, the government restored electricity within hours after residents blocked Avenue 23 following 48 hours without power, water, or gas, although State Security detained two mothers linked to that protest. In Regla, authorities sent a water truck following a similar mobilization.
The neighborhood has a history of such incidents: In June, residents engaged in pot-banging protests due to blackouts lasting up to 20 hours daily, and activist Andy García Lorenzo was detained on August 30 for filming these demonstrations in public.
This episode occurred days after the eighth total blackout of the National Electric System this year, recorded on September 18. According to the Cuban Observatory of Conflicts, July 2026 set a historic record with 1,415 protests, complaints, and critical expressions, making 2026 the year with the highest number of protests since the events of July 11, 2021.
Understanding the Ongoing Power Struggles in Cuba
What triggered the protests in El Condado?
The protests were triggered by a faulty transformer that left several blocks without electricity for almost 36 hours, despite previous reports to the Electric Company.
How did the authorities respond to the protests?
The authorities sent a technical crew to repair the transformer after residents blocked streets and built barricades, demonstrating that protests were necessary to prompt action.
Are there concerns about the durability of the repairs?
Yes, residents like Hernández Sosa expressed skepticism about the longevity of the repairs, citing the deteriorating infrastructure and lack of structural solutions.

title: Épouser une Russe en 2026 : la paperasse, pas le fantasme
content:
Épouser une Russe en 2026 : la paperasse, pas le fantasme
Visas, justificatifs, traductions, voyages via Istanbul : former un couple entre la Belgique et la Russie est devenu un parcours administratif. Loin des clichés, celles et ceux qui s'y engagent font un choix plus réfléchi que bien des couples formés au coin d'une rue.
- Publié le 20-09-2026 à 16h01
Une carte blanche de Valentin Le Normand, entrepreneur français installé à Moscou depuis 2022, fondateur de l'agence matrimoniale internationale Valentin Love
Depuis quatre ans, je dirige à Moscou une agence matrimoniale qui présente des femmes russes et biélorusses à des hommes d'Europe de l'Ouest. Quand je dis mon métier à Bruxelles ou à Paris, on me parle de passeports, de femmes soumises ou d'hommes naïfs. Personne ne me parle jamais de ce qui occupe réellement mes journées : les formulaires.
Américains et Britanniques sont exclus du dispositif
Un couple belgo-russe ou franco-russe, en 2026, est d'abord une épreuve de patience administrative, et elle commence avant la première rencontre. Pour aller la voir, un Belge, comme un Français, obtient un visa électronique en quelques jours, cinquante-deux dollars, trente jours sur place. Ses amis américains ou britanniques n'ont pas cette chance : leurs passeports sont exclus du dispositif et passent par le consulat, avec bon de réservation, assurance et rendez-vous physique. Ensuite il faut y aller. Il n'y a plus de vol direct entre l'Union européenne et la Russie. On passe par Istanbul, on compte une journée de voyage, et l'on arrive avec des cartes bancaires qui ne fonctionnent pas sur place, donc avec du liquide.
Elle doit fournir des preuves qu'elle a une raison de rentrer : un emploi, un bail, un enfant scolarisé
Dans l'autre sens, c'est plus dur. Pour qu'elle vienne en Belgique, il faut un visa Schengen de court séjour déposé chez un prestataire à Moscou ou à Saint-Pétersbourg, avec un engagement de prise en charge validé par la commune, un justificatif de domicile et les revenus de celui qui l'accueille, une assurance couvrant trente mille euros de frais médicaux, et surtout des preuves qu'elle a une raison de rentrer : un emploi, un bail, un enfant scolarisé. Le motif de refus le plus courant n'est pas la fraude, c'est un dossier qui ne démontre pas assez l'intention de retour. Un profil solide, emploi stable, appartement, enfant, peut être refusé pour dix jours de vacances parce qu'une pièce manque.
En Belgique, si le mariage se célèbre à la commune, l'officier de l'état civil peut demander l'avis du parquet avant de le célébrer.
Le mariage lui-même se prépare des deux côtés. En Belgique, si le mariage se célèbre à la commune, l'officier de l'état civil peut demander l'avis du parquet avant de le célébrer ; s'il se célèbre en Russie, le futur époux demande d'abord à son ambassade un certificat de non-empêchement à mariage. En Russie, l'état civil exige des documents apostillés et traduits par un traducteur assermenté. Si la cérémonie a lieu là-bas, l'épouse dépose ensuite une demande de visa de regroupement familial, le dossier passe par l'ambassade puis par l'Office des étrangers, et l'on compte en mois, pas en semaines. Pendant ce temps, le couple vit à distance, et les applications d'appel que l'on utilise en Europe ne fonctionnent plus toutes là-bas.
La femme qui vient nous voir a en moyenne quarante-deux ans. Plus de neuf sur dix ont un diplôme du supérieur, deux sur trois parlent anglais, une sur onze parle français
Alors pourquoi le font-ils ? Parce que le fantasme, dans cette histoire, est du côté de ceux qui n'ont jamais regardé les chiffres. La femme qui vient nous voir a en moyenne quarante-deux ans. Plus de neuf sur dix ont un diplôme du supérieur, deux sur trois parlent anglais, une sur onze parle français. Près de neuf sur dix ont déjà un enfant, exactement comme les Russes de leur génération : le recensement de 2021 compte 86 % de mères parmi les femmes de trente-cinq à trente-neuf ans. Elle s'est mariée vers vingt-cinq ans, elle a eu son premier enfant à vingt-six, elle a divorcé entre trente et trente-quatre. Elle n'a pas besoin d'un passeport, elle a un métier. Elle cherche un homme qui reste.
Un homme en moyenne entre 40 et 55 ans
L'homme, de son côté, n'est pas celui qu'on imagine non plus. Il a entre quarante et cinquante-cinq ans, souvent un divorce derrière lui, une maison, une carrière, et une lassitude des applications où l'on compare des visages sans jamais rencontrer personne. Les femmes de notre base disent chercher un homme de trente-huit à cinquante-deux ans. Ces deux populations se ressemblent bien plus qu'on ne le croit. Elles sont séparées par plus de deux mille kilomètres et une pile de formulaires.
Je ne plaide pas pour que l'administration ferme les yeux. Les contrôles existent parce que des abus existent, et des professionnels sérieux ont intérêt à ce qu'ils existent. Je plaide pour que l'on cesse de parler de ces couples comme d'une anomalie. Un mariage belgo-russe en 2026 demande des mois de patience, plusieurs allers-retours par Istanbul, une langue commune apprise tard et une confiance construite à distance. Ceux qui vont au bout ont fait un choix plus réfléchi que bien des couples formés au coin d'une rue. On peut au moins leur accorder cela : ils savent ce qu'ils font.
